extraction.name: C-EVAL: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models
extraction.description: C-EVAL is the first comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite designed to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context. It comprises 13,948 multiple-choice questions across four difficulty levels (middle school, high school, college, and professional) spanning 52 diverse disciplines ranging from humanities to science and engineering. C-EVAL is accompanied by C-EVAL HARD, a subset of very challenging subjects requiring advanced reasoning abilities, including advanced mathematics, discrete mathematics, probability and statistics, college chemistry, college physics, high school mathematics, high school chemistry, and high school physics.
extraction.creator: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He (Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tsinghua University, University of Edinburgh, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology)
extraction.publisher: NeurIPS 2023 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
extraction.citeAs: Huang, Y., Bai, Y., Zhu, Z., Zhang, J., Zhang, J., Su, T., Liu, J., Lv, C., Zhang, Y., Lei, J., Fu, Y., Sun, M., & He, J. (2023). C-EVAL: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models. NeurIPS 2023 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks. arXiv:2305.08322v3.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected primarily from mock exams freely available on the internet, past exam questions from top universities in China publicly shared by students, and mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam sourced from the Weipu website (with authorization for ~2000 questions). Data was collected either from mock exams or from small-scale local exams to mitigate data contamination risks from national exams. Most samples are sourced from PDF or Microsoft Word documents rather than plain text or structured questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Primary sources include mock exams freely available on the internet (primarily as PDF or Microsoft Word documents and a minor fraction as web pages), past exam questions from top universities in China publicly shared by students, and mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam from the Weipu website. The dataset covers 52 subjects across four difficulty levels: middle school, high school, college, and professional.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions with fewer than four options were eliminated. For questions with more than four options, incorrect choices were randomly dropped to ensure exactly four choices per question. Questions were randomly split into development, validation, and test sets within each subject with a 1:9 ratio for validation to test. The development split per subject consists of five exemplars.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF documents were initially processed into text. All questions were parsed automatically when possible, and otherwise manually by the authors, into a structured format. For subjects with complex mathematical notations, manual conversion into standard LaTeX formats was performed. All questions were processed to include exactly four choices. Questions went through standard data preprocessing including deduplication and cleaning. Questions underwent several rounds of human validation by the authors, and all LaTeX notations were ensured to compile without syntax errors. At least around 200 questions were processed for each subject.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The authors manually annotated questions parsed from PDF or Word documents into structured format. For the development split, explanation data was generated by first prompting GPT-4 to generate step-by-step explanations for ground-truth answers using five human-written question-explanation pairs as few-shot examples, then manually revising the generated explanations to obtain final high-quality explanations. All LaTeX notations were validated for correct compilation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: GPT-4 API (for automated explanation generation); manual annotation by authors
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Generated explanations from GPT-4 were manually revised by authors (Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, and Junxian He) to ensure correctness and quality. Cross-validation of collected data was performed by the team of authors.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each development set item is annotated with one explanation. Each question has one correct answer label.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators are the paper authors affiliated with Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tsinghua University, University of Edinburgh, and The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 (used to generate step-by-step explanations for development set examples)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is available at https://github.com/hkust-nlp/ceval. Ground-truth labels for the development and validation splits are released publicly, while test split labels are kept private. Users submit model predictions to https://cevalbenchmark.com for automatic test accuracy evaluation. A public leaderboard is maintained on the website. Users may optionally include their submission results in the live leaderboard.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: C-EVAL is intended to help analyze important strengths and shortcomings of foundation models and foster their development and growth for Chinese users. The benchmark addresses the gap between Chinese LLM development and evaluation, providing a tool for developers to understand model abilities from multiple dimensions. It aims to guide LLM development beyond casual conversational bots toward more complex scenarios relevant to Chinese society.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: English benchmarks tend to exhibit geographical biases towards the domestic knowledge of the regions that produce them. C-EVAL was specifically designed to include Chinese cultural, historical, and legal knowledge relevant to Chinese users. There are minor fluctuations in the distribution of correct answer options (A: 22.9%, B: 26.0%, C: 26.4%, D: 24.7%), similar in magnitude to MMLU.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: C-EVAL, along with all English-language benchmarks, is far from perfect for LLM evaluation. It does not cover many other abilities such as reasoning over and calling APIs, and does not assess multiple aspects beyond accuracy including safety, bias, and robustness. The benchmark is limited to multiple-choice format. The middle school English subject and middle school Chinese subject (which mostly focuses on writing responses) were excluded. The validation set contains fewer than 30 questions per subject on average, making subject-level accuracy tracking less reliable.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of large language models' advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities in a Chinese context. The benchmark supports zero-shot and few-shot evaluation in both answer-only and chain-of-thought settings. Subsets can be separately utilized to assess certain model abilities of interest. The validation set is intended for hyperparameter tuning. The test set is used for fair model comparison via the online submission system.
